risks: Rising costs, supply disruptions, and import restrictions on essential raw materials may impact our expenses, timelines, and overall financial performance.
The prices of our primary raw materials, including those imported for the production of Adhesive Tapes, Polishing and Buffing Pads, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds have been volatile.
We source raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro for our manufacturing operations from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers.

Raw materials used in the manufacturing of Adhesive Tapes, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds, and Buffing Pads are global commodities, and their prices tend to be cyclical, fluctuating in response to global market conditions.
Our raw materials are imported from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey.

If the costs of these raw materials rise due to factors such as rise in input and commodity prices or shortages in supply, and our Company is not able to recover these costs through cost saving measures elsewhere or by increasing the prices of its products, our results of operations could be adversely affected.
In the event prices for these raw materials subsequently decline there can be no assurance that our Company will be able to price our products based on the material costs it actually incurred.
Our Registered Office and Manufacturing unit from where we operate is not owned by us.

business_ops.seasonality: Per the DRHP: 'Our business is dependent to a certain extent on the seasonal, environmental and climate changes. Hence, our business is seasonal in nature.'
business_ops.supply_chain_integration: The Company describes itself as operating both a manufacturing division (adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes, domes and graphics, car care products) and a trading division (tools, abrasives, body shop consumables, retail products, accessories and aerosols), so a portion of what it sells is bought-in rather than made. On the inbound side it is not backward integrated: raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro are sourced from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers, with imports from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, the United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey; the cost of raw material consumed represented 37.01%, 43.26%, 44.29% and 47.10% of total revenues in the period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively. Conversion is done in-house at two manufacturing units (Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu and IMT Manesar, Haryana) using UV machines, dome machines, filling machines, label printing machines, shrink tunnels, pre-tape masking paper machines, masker roller machines, die-punching machines and cone high-lift pallet trucks, with an in-house testing laboratory and an R&D team; the Company states it is among the few with in-line doming application units. Outbound, the Company states it operates a Kanban / Just-in-Time inventory system to minimise stock levels, and reaches market through a dual-segment route: direct long-term B2B supply to automotive OEMs, and distributors, e-commerce platforms and direct sales for the B2C/B2B refinish market.

overview.business_model: Two streams. The manufacturing division produces adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes and printing solutions, domes and graphics, and a range of car care products, made at Unit I (SIPCOT Industrial Park, Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu) and Unit II (IMT Manesar, Haryana) under ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certifications, with customisation offered to clients. The trading segment resells electrical and pneumatic tools, abrasive sheets, discs and rolls, body shop consumables, retail products and accessories, and aerosol products. Customers are automotive OEMs and the aftermarket/refinish trade: the DRHP states that sales to Automotive Industry suppliers accounted for 100% in each of Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 and the period ended September 30, 2025, and that top-10 customers contributed 52.67%, 46.43%, 43.92% and 44.35% of total sales in the period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively. The working-capital cycle lengthens in every period: debtor days 34 to 38 to 41 to 49, inventory days 56 to 61 to 64 to 72, while creditor days move 18 to 18 to 16 to 20, so the funding is coming from the Company rather than from suppliers.

verdict.our_read: Sumax Engineering Limited is a 1994-incorporated, Secunderabad-headquartered converter and trader of automotive adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, domes and graphics and car-care products, with a bought-in trading line of tools, abrasives, body-shop consumables and aerosols, made at two units at SIPCOT Sriperumbudur (Tamil Nadu) and IMT Manesar (Haryana) under ISO 9001:2015, IATF 16949:2016, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018. All figures in the DRHP are printed '(Rs In Lakhs)'. Scale is small: revenue from operations of ₹12,682.09, ₹13,079.45 and ₹14,612.60 lakhs in FY23, FY24 and FY25 (FY25 = ₹146.13 crore) and ₹7,174.69 lakhs in H1FY26, with EBITDA margin climbing 6.32% to 8.84% to 10.21% to 11.80% and restated PAT of ₹464.44, ₹744.02, ₹999.32 and ₹580.02 lakhs (FY25 PAT = ₹9.99 crore). The revenue base is undiversified by end-market — the DRHP states sales to Automotive Industry suppliers were 100% in each of FY23, FY24, FY25 and the period ended September 30, 2025 — with top-10 customers at 44.35%, 43.92%, 46.43% and 52.67% and no firm-commitment agreements with any of them, and adhesive tapes and die-cuts at 45.00% of the H1FY26 mix. Inputs are the mirror image: raw material consumed was 47.10%, 44.29%, 43.26% and 37.01% of total revenues, and Annexure XLIII shows the imported share of consumption rising 65.97% / 65.45% / 66.20% / 84.92%, sourced across twelve countries, with foreign-currency expenditure of ₹3,727.99 lakhs in H1FY26 alone. Returns look high on a thin asset base (RoCE 19.70% / 23.32% / 24.63%, RoNW 14.75% / 19.11% / 20.42%, net fixed assets of only ₹698.13 lakhs against FY25 revenue), but FY25 cash flow from operations was ₹69.98 lakhs against that ₹999.32 lakh PAT, after an inventory build of ₹590.56 lakhs, a receivables build of ₹418.48 lakhs and income tax paid of ₹361.77 lakhs. The Offer is up to 53,00,000 Equity Shares of ₹10 — a Fresh Issue of up to 43,00,000 shares on a pre-Offer base of 1,47,31,500 shares, plus an Offer for Sale of up to 10,00,000 shares entirely by Mr. Sudeep Mehta (9,00,000) and Mrs. Vimla Mehta (1,00,000), whose proceeds go to them and not to the Company, and an employee reservation of up to 2,10,000 shares — on NSE Emerge. Identified Fresh Issue objects total ₹3,351.02 lakhs by my addition: ₹488.68 lakhs of building at a proposed Unit I at Tapukara, Rajasthan, ₹1,662.34 lakhs of building at a proposed Unit II at MET Jhajjar, Haryana, and ₹1,200.00 lakhs of working capital in FY2026-27, with general corporate purposes, the Offer Price, post-Issue capital and every P/E cell printed as placeholders. Land for both units (₹957.00 and ₹1,329.56 lakhs, ₹2,286.56 lakhs by my addition) is stated as already acquired and incurred with Nil IPO funding, while the DRHP also states no amount had been deployed towards the objects till September 30, 2025 — a date at which net fixed assets stood at ₹760.63 lakhs. Ownership is 100% Promoter and Promoter Group across 7 shareholders, with the entire 38,10,000-share Minimum Promoter's Contribution coming from a 6:1 bonus allotted on March 11, 2026, nineteen days before this March 30, 2026 filing, for consideration other than cash; the securities premium account before the Issue is Nil; and the issuer states twice that it has no comparable listed peers in India, so the document carries no peer P/E, no peer accounting-ratio comparison and no market-share figure.

Against that, the DRHP discloses no market share and no competitive rank, describes its market only as having 'limited numbers of operators', states twice that there are no comparable listed peers in India, and confirms it holds no firm-commitment agreements with customers. Adhesive tapes and die-cuts are 45.00% of the H1FY26 mix, while traded lines (abrasives 24.12%, tools 1.69%, body-shop consumables 1.78%, retail 0.04%, aerosols 0.09%) are 27.72% of H1FY26 revenue by my addition of the printed line percentages, so a material part of what is sold is resold rather than made.

Printed RoCE of 19.70% / 23.32% / 24.63% and RoNW of 14.75% / 19.11% / 20.42% for FY23-FY25, on a net fixed asset base of ₹726.26 / ₹687.45 / ₹698.13 lakhs — an asset-light conversion structure where the return is being earned on working capital rather than on plant. Litigation exposure is narrow and directed outward: Nil criminal proceedings against the Company, Nil material civil litigation against it, Nil actions by statutory or regulatory authorities, and Nil in every category for Promoters, other Directors and KMP/SMP; the Company's own two proceedings (Commercial Suit 63 of 2025 for ₹160.00 lakhs and FIR 123/2025) are against a former employee and connected parties, not related parties.

Two of the three independent directors bring directly relevant records — Mr. Vinay Kumar Piparsania with 30 years in automotive and mobility (Ford India, Hero Corporate Service, TVS Automobile Solutions) and Mr. Vijay S Bapna, an FCA with prior Chairman and Audit Committee roles at listed companies (Usha Martin, MMP Industries, Lagnam Spintex).

products.title: Products (RHP)
products.body:
- Manufactured range for the Automotive OEM and Auto Refinish markets; die-cuts used mainly for bumper masking in cars and two-wheelers. The Company states it is among the few with in-line doming application units, producing domed labels in acrylic for consumer-durables and domed emblems for automotive and white goods.
- Traded segment supplying the automotive aftermarket / refinish channel.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: The Company describes itself as operating both a manufacturing division (adhesive tapes and die-cuts, pre-taped masking film, rubbing and polishing compounds, buffing and foam pads, reflective tapes, domes and graphics, car care products) and a trading division (tools, abrasives, body shop consumables, retail products, accessories and aerosols), so a portion of what it sells is bought-in rather than made. On the inbound side it is not backward integrated: raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro are sourced from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers, with imports from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, the United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey; the cost of raw material consumed represented 37.01%, 43.26%, 44.29% and 47.10% of total revenues in the period ended September 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2025, 2024 and 2023 respectively. Conversion is done in-house at two manufacturing units (Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu and IMT Manesar, Haryana) using UV machines, dome machines, filling machines, label printing machines, shrink tunnels, pre-tape masking paper machines, masker roller machines, die-punching machines and cone high-lift pallet trucks, with an in-house testing laboratory and an R&D team; the Company states it is among the few with in-line doming application units. Outbound, the Company states it operates a Kanban / Just-in-Time inventory system to minimise stock levels, and reaches market through a dual-segment route: direct long-term B2B supply to automotive OEMs, and distributors, e-commerce platforms and direct sales for the B2C/B2B refinish market.

demand_drivers.title: Seasonality (RHP report)
demand_drivers.body: Per the DRHP: 'Our business is dependent to a certain extent on the seasonal, environmental and climate changes. Hence, our business is seasonal in nature.'

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Rising costs, supply disruptions, and import restrictions on essential raw materials may impact our expenses, timelines, and overall financial performance.
- The prices of our primary raw materials, including those imported for the production of Adhesive Tapes, Polishing and Buffing Pads, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds have been volatile.
- We source raw materials such as Jumbo Rolls, Solvents, Skins, Heat Film and Velcro for our manufacturing operations from a combination of domestic and foreign suppliers.
- Raw materials used in the manufacturing of Adhesive Tapes, Rubbing and Polishing Compounds, and Buffing Pads are global commodities, and their prices tend to be cyclical, fluctuating in response to global market conditions.
- Our raw materials are imported from China, Japan, Portugal, Taiwan, United States of America, Spain, Thailand, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, Malaysia and Turkey.
- If the costs of these raw materials rise due to factors such as rise in input and commodity prices or shortages in supply, and our Company is not able to recover these costs through cost saving measures elsewhere or by increasing the prices of its products, our results of operations could be adversely affected.
- In the event prices for these raw materials subsequently decline there can be no assurance that our Company will be able to price our products based on the material costs it actually incurred.
- Our Registered Office and Manufacturing unit from where we operate is not owned by us.
